library.description: Singleton micro-frontend hub: contract-first shared state, owner-scoped events and requests, plugin-based persistence for Module Federation and Web Components.

blocks.text: English
微前端（Module Federation remote 与 Web Components）之间的通信与共享存储。整个页面只有一个 hub：主应用创建它，主应用和每个子应用用同样的 `connect(name)` 拿到同形状的句柄，再通过契约读写状态、收发事件、发起请求。
社区方案大多只解决一个切面：qiankun 的 `initGlobalState` 是一个整体对象，任何变化都回调所有应用；事件总线没有当前值，晚到的订阅方直接丢事件；Module Federation 共享 zustand / redux 时，任何应用都能改任何状态。micro-hub 把这几件事放进一个模型：

items: 每份状态有 owner。 一个契约同一时刻只有一个 owner；只有 owner 和契约里列出的 `writers` 能写，其它应用只能读。出了问题能定位是谁改的。
契约带类型和版本。 两个独立部署的应用对同一契约的主版本不一致时，`use()` 直接报 `CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH`，不会静默错乱。
卸载即干净。 `disconnect()` 一次性释放这个应用登记的所有订阅、handler 和所有权，重挂载不会出现重复回调或幽灵回调。
按需通知。 每个字段、每个实体 id、每个 `select()` 结果都是独立的订阅点；一次命令里的多个写入只通知一次。
命令同步提交。 command 是同步纯函数，不会出现跨 `await` 的丢失更新。
同 realm 零拷贝。 不序列化、不 postMessage；提交的值顶层冻结，防止别的应用就地修改。
插件化。 只要通信就装 `events()`，只要状态就装 `state()`，需要持久化再加 `persist()`。
与框架无关。 对外只有 `get()` + `subscribe()`，React、Vue、Svelte、Solid、Angular、原生 Web Components 都能几行接入。

blocks.text: 适用：同一个页面（同一个 JS realm）里的多个应用——Module Federation 加载的 remote、以 Web Component 形式挂载的子应用、主应用本身。
不适用：

items: iframe、Worker、跨标签页：这些是不同的 realm，用 `@migaia/rpc-plugin-browser`。
页面内单个应用自己的状态：直接用 `@migaia/store-keyed` 或 `@migaia/store-light`。

blocks.text: 需要共享异步值时再装可选 peer `@migaia/resource`；持久化需要一个存储后端，例如 `storage.backend.browser`。
hub 必须是整页唯一的一份。主应用和每个 remote 都把它声明为 singleton：

如果某个 remote 的 `requiredVersion` 超出主应用提供的版本范围，Module Federation 会退回到这个 remote 自带的副本，两边的事件和状态就会静默分裂。上线前确认所有应用的版本范围一致。入口使用异步边界（`import('./bootstrap')`），避免 "Shared module is not available for eager consumption"。

sections.id: 1-定义契约-由-owner-团队维护-通过-mf-expose-共享
sections.heading: 1. 定义契约（由 owner 团队维护，通过 MF expose 共享）

blocks.code:
import { createMicroHub } from '@migaia/micro-hub'
import { events } from '@migaia/micro-hub/events'
import { state } from '@migaia/micro-hub/state'
import { persist } from '@migaia/micro-hub/persist'
import { localStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/local-storage'

createMicroHub({
  plugins: [events(), state(), persist({ store: localStorageHost({ namespace: 'shop' }) })]
})

blocks.text: `IReadable` 只有 `get()` 和 `subscribe()`：`get()` 在下一次提交前返回同一个引用；通知不带值，回调里调用 `get()` 拿到的已经是新值。
子应用以自定义元素挂载时，可以不经全局变量拿到 app 句柄。`@migaia/micro-hub/web-component` 实现了社区 Context Protocol 的 `context-request` 事件，Lit 的 `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT })` 也能直接用：

`consumeMicroApp` 比 provider 先挂载时，请求会等待，provider 出现后补发应答。外部 Lit consumer 若可能先挂载，应在共同祖先连接 `ContextRoot` 并使用 `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT, subscribe: true })`；`provideMicroApp` 发出可跨 shadow DOM 的 `context-provider` 事件，触发 ContextRoot 重放早到请求。
契约用到了没装的插件时，`use()` / `own()` 报 `PLUGIN_MISSING`；插件依赖没装时，`createMicroHub()` 报 `PLUGIN_MISSING`，hub 不会被创建。

所有错误带 `source: '@migaia/micro-hub'` 和 `code`（`MicroHubErrorCode`）：`HUB_ALREADY_CREATED`、`HUB_NOT_CREATED`、`APP_ALREADY_CONNECTED`、`APP_DISCONNECTED`、`PLUGIN_MISSING`、`CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH`、`CONTRACT_OWNED`、`WRITE_DENIED`、`EMIT_DENIED`、`COMMAND_ASYNC`、`HANDLER_DUPLICATED`、`OWNER_ABSENT`、`OWNER_TIMEOUT`、`OWNER_GONE`、`INVALID_OPTION`。每个码的触发条件与处理方式见 USEGUIDE。
需要按错误分支时，比较 `error.source === MICRO_HUB_SOURCE` 和 `error.code`，不要匹配消息文字。`MicroHubErrorText` 导出全部消息文字，测试或日志需要核对原文时引用它。
listener 和订阅回调抛出的错误不会打断其它 listener，也不会抛给 emit 方，而是交给 `createMicroHub({ report })`（默认 `globalThis.reportError`）。

blocks.text: `report(error)` 接收不应打断当前操作的错误：listener 和订阅回调的异常、清理失败。省略时使用 `globalThis.reportError`，没有则 `console.error`。`report` 自身抛错时，两个错误都交给默认 reporter。

rows: 正整数主版本。同名契约以第一次登记的版本为准，之后版本不同报 `CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH`。

`(state) => value`。只依赖它实际读取的字段。
`(state, ...args) => patch`。必须同步；返回只包含要改的字段。

items: `get()` 在下一次提交前返回同一个引用。
`subscribe(listener)` 在之后每次提交后调用 `listener()`，不传值；回调里 `get()` 已是新值。返回的取消函数可重复调用；应用断开时自动取消。
一次 command 写多个字段，所有订阅者在同一批次后各收到一次通知。
keyed 字段写某个 id，只通知这个 id 的订阅者；id 增删时 `ids` 才通知。

blocks.text: `commands.<name>(...args)` 返回 `{ revision }`。调用方既不是 owner 也不在 `writers` 中时报 `WRITE_DENIED`。command 返回 thenable 时报 `COMMAND_ASYNC`（`TypeError`），状态不变。patch 中出现契约里没有的字段报 `INVALID_OPTION`，同样不写入任何字段。
`select(selector, equals?)` 返回 `IReadable<R>`：只有 `equals`（默认 `Object.is`）判定结果变化时才通知；未订阅时 `get()` 按 revision 缓存，结果相等时保持旧引用。最后一个订阅者离开时释放内部节点。
`revision` 是契约的提交次数。

items: `events.<name>.on(listener)`：返回取消函数，断开时自动取消。
owner 的 `emit` 同步分发，listener 按注册顺序调用；listener 中再次 emit 会排队，在当前分发结束后执行。单次顶层 emit 最多触发 `publishBudget`（默认 10 000）次 listener 调用，超过时停止并上报，避免两个应用互相 emit 形成死循环。
listener 抛出的错误交给 `report`，不影响其它 listener，也不抛给 emit 方。

blocks.text: `requests.<name>(input, { waitForOwner? })`：

items: owner 已注册 handler：调用它，返回 handler 的结果；handler 抛出的错误原样拒绝。
没有 handler 且未设置 `waitForOwner`：拒绝 `OWNER_ABSENT`。
设置了 `waitForOwner`：等待 handler 注册；超时拒绝 `OWNER_TIMEOUT`；等待期间调用方断开拒绝 `APP_DISCONNECTED`。
调用进行中 owner 断开或 `release()`：拒绝 `OWNER_GONE`。handler 的副作用可能已经发生，重试前先对账。

blocks.text: `persist({ store, debounceMs?, keyPrefix? })` 需要 `state()`。`store` 是任意 `IKeyValueStore`，例如 `@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/local-storage` 的 `localStorageHost({ namespace })` 或 `@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/indexed-db` 的 `indexedDbHost({ dbName })`。这两个工厂名字带 `Host`，但只返回一个 store，不会创建 storage-plugin-browser 的 host；micro-hub 也不使用 storage-plugin-browser 的 `./plugins/*`（它们只能装进 storage host）。hub 只借用这个 store，不会释放它。

`own(contract, { persist: ['items'], persistKey? })` 把所选普通字段写到 `<keyPrefix><persistKey ?? 契约名>`，并在 owner 启动时读回。读回期间发生的写入不会被存档覆盖（store-persist 的 hydrate 合并规则）。同一 hub 内更换 owner 时，已恢复或已写入的字段保留内存值，不再被旧存档覆盖；新 hub 仍会恢复存档。存档版本取契约 `version`；主版本升级后旧存档被丢弃，字段从契约初始值开始。`owned.persistence.ready` 在首次读回成功后兑现。owner 断开或 `release()` 时停止持久化。keyed 字段不能持久化。
同一 hub、同一存储 key 的异步写入在 owner 交接时保持顺序：新 attachment 的读写与删除等待前任已接纳的写入及最终写入完成，因此 `persistence.ready` 可能等待前任释放。`hub.dispose()` 也等待这些写入结束；失败交给 hub 的 `report`，不阻止下一任恢复读写。
`resources()` 需要可选 peer `@migaia/resource`。owner 调用 `provide(name, (signal) => fetch(...))` 后：

items: `resources.<name>.read()`：已有值直接兑现；请求中返回同一个 Promise；否则发起请求。并发读取共享一次请求。
`resources.<name>.state`：`IReadable<{ status, data, error }>`。订阅会开始观察资源。
`resources.<name>.refetch()`：丢弃缓存重新请求；失败交给 `report`。
owner 未提供时 `read()` 拒绝 `OWNER_ABSENT`，`state.get()` 为 `idle`。

rows: Context Protocol 的 context key（字符串）。
让 `element` 应答后代（含 shadow DOM）的 `context-request`；同时应答此前未被应答的 helper 请求，并发出 `context-provider` 以便外部 ContextRoot 重放订阅请求。返回停止函数。
发出 `context-request`（`bubbles`、`composed`）；没有 provider 时等待。返回取消函数。

blocks.text: Lit consumer 可能早于 provider 连接时，在共同祖先先连接 `ContextRoot`，并设置 `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT, subscribe: true })`。ContextRoot 记录未应答的订阅请求，收到 provider 的 `context-provider` 后从原 consumer 重新发出请求；本包复用这一协议，不创建自己的 ContextRoot。

items: 每个应用是 hub 内部 plugin-host 中的一个插件；`disconnect()` 先同步释放资源，再异步卸载插件，因此卸载过程中不会有回调到达已卸载的应用。立即以同名重新连接是允许的。

blocks.text: 中文

Communication and shared state between micro-frontends (Module Federation remotes and Web Components). A page has exactly one hub: the shell creates it, and the shell and every child app call the same `connect(name)` to get a handle of the same shape. Through contracts, apps read and write state, send and receive events, and make requests.

Most community solutions cover only one part of the problem. qiankun's `initGlobalState` is one big object, and every change calls back every app. An event bus has no current value, so a subscriber that arrives late misses the event. Sharing zustand or redux through Module Federation lets any app change any state. micro-hub puts these concerns into one model:

items: Every piece of state has an owner. A contract has one owner at a time. Only the owner and the apps listed in the contract's `writers` can write; other apps can only read. When something goes wrong, you can tell which app changed it.
Contracts are typed and versioned. When two independently deployed apps disagree on a contract's major version, `use()` throws `CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH` instead of silently mixing data.
Unmounting leaves nothing behind. `disconnect()` releases every subscription, handler and ownership the app registered, in one call. Remounting does not produce duplicate or stale callbacks.
Notifications only where needed. Each field, each entity id and each `select()` result is its own subscription point. Several writes in one command notify once.
Commands commit synchronously. A command is a synchronous pure function, so no update is lost across an `await`.
Zero copies within one realm. Nothing is serialized and nothing goes through postMessage. Committed values are frozen at the top level so another app cannot modify them in place.
Plugins. Install `events()` if you only need messaging, `state()` if you only need state, and add `persist()` when you need persistence.
Framework-neutral. The public surface is `get()` plus `subscribe()`, so React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular and plain Web Components connect in a few lines.

blocks.text: Use it for several apps on the same page (the same JS realm): remotes loaded through Module Federation, child apps mounted as Web Components, and the shell itself.
Do not use it for:

items: iframes, Workers, or other browser tabs. These are separate realms; use `@migaia/rpc-plugin-browser`.
State that belongs to a single app on the page. Use `@migaia/store-keyed` or `@migaia/store-light` directly.

blocks.text: Install the optional peer `@migaia/resource` only when you share asynchronous values. Persistence needs a storage backend, for example `storage.backend.browser`.
The hub must be a single copy for the whole page. Declare it as a singleton in the shell and in every remote:

If a remote's `requiredVersion` falls outside the range the shell provides, Module Federation falls back to the remote's own copy, and events and state silently split in two. Check that every app uses the same version range before release. Use an async boundary for the entry (`import('./bootstrap')`) to avoid "Shared module is not available for eager consumption".

sections.heading: 1. Define a contract (maintained by the owner team and shared through an MF expose)
2. Create the hub in the shell

blocks.code:
import { createMicroHub } from '@migaia/micro-hub'
import { events } from '@migaia/micro-hub/events'
import { state } from '@migaia/micro-hub/state'
import { persist } from '@migaia/micro-hub/persist'
import { localStorageHost } from '@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/local-storage'

createMicroHub({
  plugins: [events(), state(), persist({ store: localStorageHost({ namespace: 'shop' }) })]
})

sections.heading: 3. Connect each app (the shell and child apps use the same code)

blocks.text: `IReadable` has only `get()` and `subscribe()`. `get()` returns the same reference until the next commit. Notifications carry no value; calling `get()` inside the callback already returns the new value.

When a child app is mounted as a custom element, it can get its app handle without a global variable. `@migaia/micro-hub/web-component` implements the `context-request` event of the community Context Protocol, so Lit's `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT })` works as well:

When `consumeMicroApp` is mounted before the provider, the request waits and is answered once the provider appears. If an external Lit consumer may mount first, connect a `ContextRoot` on a common ancestor and use `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT, subscribe: true })`. `provideMicroApp` dispatches a `context-provider` event that crosses shadow DOM, which makes the ContextRoot replay early requests.

When a contract uses a plugin that is not installed, `use()` / `own()` throws `PLUGIN_MISSING`. When a plugin's own dependency is not installed, `createMicroHub()` throws `PLUGIN_MISSING` and no hub is created.

Every error carries `source: '@migaia/micro-hub'` and a `code` (`MicroHubErrorCode`): `HUB_ALREADY_CREATED`, `HUB_NOT_CREATED`, `APP_ALREADY_CONNECTED`, `APP_DISCONNECTED`, `PLUGIN_MISSING`, `CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH`, `CONTRACT_OWNED`, `WRITE_DENIED`, `EMIT_DENIED`, `COMMAND_ASYNC`, `HANDLER_DUPLICATED`, `OWNER_ABSENT`, `OWNER_TIMEOUT`, `OWNER_GONE`, `INVALID_OPTION`. See the USEGUIDE for when each code is thrown and what to do.

To branch on an error, compare `error.source === MICRO_HUB_SOURCE` and `error.code`; do not match the message text. `MicroHubErrorText` exports every message; refer to it when a test or a log needs to check the exact wording.
Errors thrown by listeners and subscription callbacks do not stop other listeners and do not reach the emitter. They go to `createMicroHub({ report })`, which defaults to `globalThis.reportError`.

`hub.dispose()` disconnects every app and returns `Promise<void>` for app unloading and hub cleanup; later disposal calls on that hub reuse its disposal Promise. `createMicroHub` can be called again afterwards.

blocks.text: `report(error)` receives errors that must not interrupt the current operation: exceptions from listeners and subscription callbacks, and cleanup failures. When omitted, the hub uses `globalThis.reportError`, or `console.error` when that is missing. If `report` itself throws, both errors go to the default reporter.
`defineContract(name, spec)` only validates and freezes; it has no side effects. The hub registers a contract the first time an app calls `use()` or `own()` with it.

rows: Positive integer major version. The first registration of a name decides the version; a different version later throws `CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH`.
Initial field values, or `keyed<T>()`. Initial values are copied with `structuredClone` and frozen at the top level, so they must be structured-cloneable.
`(state) => value`. Depends only on the fields it actually reads.
`(state, ...args) => patch`. Must be synchronous; the patch contains only the fields to change.
Apps other than the owner that may call commands. By default only the owner can write.
`request<In, Out>()`. The owner registers exactly one handler.

blocks.text: Invalid names, versions that are not positive integers, and section members of the wrong kind throw `INVALID_OPTION` (`TypeError`).

rows: The app name; `connected` becomes false after `disconnect()`.
Returns the contract view. Repeated calls by the same app for the same contract return the same object.
Claims ownership and returns the view plus the owner-only members. Throws `CONTRACT_OWNED` when the contract already has an owner.

The app's `disconnect()` synchronously releases its subscriptions, handlers and ownership, then returns `Promise<void>` for unloading its plugin from plugin-host; later disconnection calls on that app reuse this unloading Promise.

blocks.text: After disconnecting, calling any member of the handle or a view throws `APP_DISCONNECTED`. Owner-only members:

rows: Registers a request handler; registering twice throws `HANDLER_DUPLICATED`. Returns an unregister function.
Registers the fetcher of a shared asynchronous value. Returns an unregister function.
The store-persist `IPersistHandle` when persistence was requested, otherwise `undefined`.
Gives up ownership so another app can claim it. The state is kept.

blocks.text: On a view, `state.<field>` is an `IReadable<T>`; a `keyed` field is `{ at(id): IReadable<T | undefined>; ids: IReadable<readonly string[]> }`.

items: `get()` returns the same reference until the next commit.

`subscribe(listener)` calls `listener()` after every later commit, without a value; `get()` inside the callback already returns the new value. The returned cancel function can be called more than once, and cancellation happens automatically when the app disconnects.
When one command writes several fields, every subscriber is notified once, after the whole batch.
Writing one id of a keyed field notifies only that id's subscribers; `ids` notifies only when ids are added or removed.

blocks.text: `commands.<name>(...args)` returns `{ revision }`. Throws `WRITE_DENIED` when the caller is neither the owner nor listed in `writers`. Throws `COMMAND_ASYNC` (`TypeError`) when the command returns a thenable, and the state stays unchanged. A patch field that the contract does not declare throws `INVALID_OPTION`, and no field is written.

`select(selector, equals?)` returns an `IReadable<R>`. It notifies only when `equals` (default `Object.is`) reports a changed result. While nobody subscribes, `get()` caches by revision and keeps the old reference when the result is equal. The internal node is released when the last subscriber leaves.
`revision` counts the commits of the contract.

items: `events.<name>.on(listener)` returns a cancel function; cancellation happens automatically on disconnect.

The owner's `emit` delivers synchronously, calling listeners in registration order. An emit made inside a listener is queued and runs after the current delivery finishes. One top-level emit can cause at most `publishBudget` (default 10 000) listener calls; beyond that, delivery stops and the overflow is reported. This prevents two apps that emit in reaction to each other from looping forever.
Errors thrown by a listener go to `report`. They do not affect other listeners and are not thrown to the emitter.

blocks.text: `requests.<name>(input, { waitForOwner? })`:

items: When the owner has registered a handler, it is called and its result is returned; an error thrown by the handler rejects the call unchanged.
When there is no handler and `waitForOwner` is not set, the call rejects with `OWNER_ABSENT`.
When `waitForOwner` is set, the call waits for a handler to be registered. It rejects with `OWNER_TIMEOUT` on timeout, and with `APP_DISCONNECTED` if the caller disconnects while waiting.
When the owner disconnects or calls `release()` while a call is in progress, the call rejects with `OWNER_GONE`. The handler's side effects may already have happened; reconcile before retrying.

blocks.text: `persist({ store, debounceMs?, keyPrefix? })` requires `state()`. `store` is any `IKeyValueStore`, for example `localStorageHost({ namespace })` from `@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/local-storage` or `indexedDbHost({ dbName })` from `@migaia/storage-plugin-browser/indexed-db`. Despite the `Host` in their names, these two factories return only a store and do not create a storage-plugin-browser host. micro-hub does not use storage-plugin-browser's `./plugins/*`, which can only be installed into a storage host. The hub borrows the store and never releases it.

`own(contract, { persist: ['items'], persistKey? })` writes the selected plain fields to `<keyPrefix><persistKey ?? contract name>` and reads them back when the owner starts. Writes made while reading back are not overwritten by the saved data (the store-persist hydrate merge rule). When the owner changes within the same hub, fields that were already restored or written keep their in-memory values and are not overwritten by the old saved data; a new hub still restores the saved data. The saved version is the contract `version`; after a major version upgrade the old data is discarded and the fields start from the contract's initial values. `owned.persistence.ready` resolves after the first successful read-back. Persistence stops when the owner disconnects or calls `release()`. Keyed fields cannot be persisted.

Asynchronous writes to the same storage key within one hub keep their order across an owner handover: the new attachment's reads, writes and deletes wait until the previous owner's accepted writes and final write have finished, so `persistence.ready` may wait for the previous owner to release. `hub.dispose()` also waits for these writes. Failures go to the hub's `report` and do not prevent the next owner from restoring and writing.
`resources()` requires the optional peer `@migaia/resource`. After the owner calls `provide(name, (signal) => fetch(...))`:

items: `resources.<name>.read()` resolves immediately when a value exists, returns the same Promise while a request is in progress, and starts a request otherwise. Concurrent reads share one request.
`resources.<name>.state` is an `IReadable<{ status, data, error }>`. Subscribing starts observing the resource.
`resources.<name>.refetch()` discards the cached value and requests again; failures go to `report`.
Before the owner provides a fetcher, `read()` rejects with `OWNER_ABSENT` and `state.get()` has status `idle`.

rows: The Context Protocol context key (a string).

Makes `element` answer `context-request` events from its descendants, including inside shadow DOM. It also answers helper requests that were waiting, and dispatches `context-provider` so an external ContextRoot replays its subscription requests. Returns a stop function.
Dispatches a `context-request` (`bubbles`, `composed`); waits when there is no provider yet. Returns a cancel function.

blocks.text: When a Lit consumer may connect before the provider, connect a `ContextRoot` on a common ancestor first and set `@consume({ context: MICRO_APP_CONTEXT, subscribe: true })`. ContextRoot records unanswered subscription requests and, when it receives the provider's `context-provider`, re-dispatches them from the original consumers. This module reuses that protocol and does not create a ContextRoot of its own.

items: Each app is a plugin of the hub's internal plugin-host. `disconnect()` first releases resources synchronously and then unloads the plugin asynchronously, so no callback reaches an app that is being unloaded. Reconnecting immediately with the same name is allowed.
Commands run synchronously, so they are naturally serial within one realm. A command called inside a subscription callback commits after the current batch finishes.
State is kept after the owner disconnects; a new owner can claim the contract and keep writing.

symbols.signature: export declare function provideMicroApp(element: Element, app: IMicroApp): () => void;
symbols.purpose: Makes `element` answer `context-request` events for the app handle from its descendants, including inside shadow DOM. It also answers requests that were waiting before it existed, and dispatches `context-provider` so an external Lit ContextRoot replays its early requests. Use it together with `consumeMicroApp` in the child element.
symbols.core:
element: Ancestor element of the child apps, usually the slot the shell mounts them into.
app: The handle to hand out, returned by `getMicroHub().connect(name)`.
A function that stops providing; later requests are no longer answered by this element.
